Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(bunker): protocol hardening — re-derivation, replay, active-MITM, limits

Round A of the bunker hardening follow-ups:

- Anti-smuggling re-derivation check (#4): the phone rebuilds the canonical
  CAPAUTH_NONCE_V2 from parsed fields and refuses to sign if it differs from the
  relayed payload — a malicious desktop can't get a friendly origin approved
  while signing different/extra bytes.
- Replay protection (#2): the broker rejects a duplicate client request id
  (sign_request/enc) per session (`duplicate_request`).
- Active-MITM resistance (#1): an optional QR-only key fragment (`frag`, URI
  `&f=`) is mixed into the HKDF info. The broker never sees it, so it cannot
  derive the channel key even by substituting the relayed kex pubkeys. Wired
  through E2ESession (py+js), the phone URI parser, and RemoteBunkerBackend.
  Cross-impl vector extended with the frag-mixed key+ciphertext.
- Broker limits (#3): per-IP sliding-window rate limit + global session cap
  (BunkerCapacityError → 503) + optional bearer auth (CAPAUTH_BUNKER_AUTH_TOKEN)
  on POST /bunker/session.

Tests: 31 Python (bunker+e2e, incl. replay/cap/kex-enc/frag) + 88 JS — green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(bunker): E2E-encrypt the relay so the broker can't read it

The broker relayed sign_request payloads + signatures in plaintext (app
layer) — readable by the broker process, its logs/memory, or a 3rd-party
relay. Add an end-to-end channel (capauth-bunker-e2e-v1):

- Ephemeral X25519 `kex` exchanged over the relay; shared = ECDH(priv,
  peerPub); key = HKDF-SHA256(shared, salt=pairing_secret,
  info="capauth-bunker-e2e-v1", 32). Sensitive messages AES-256-GCM sealed
  inside an `enc` envelope: base64(nonce | ct | tag). Broker now relays only
  kex + enc and cannot read the payload or the signature.
- New modules: bunker_e2e.py (Python harness) and lib/bunker-e2e.js
  (WebCrypto; identical copy in extension + phone). Broker (_RELAYED_TYPES)
  gains kex/enc; clients always kex-then-enc, plaintext fallback retained.
- Wired into the phone signer loop and the desktop client backend.
- Shared cross-impl vector: Python + JS assert byte-identical HKDF+AEAD.
  Tests: 8 Python + 7 JS; full suites 84 JS / 52 Python (bunker+e2e+verifier).

Honest threat model: defeats a passive/honest-but-curious broker (+ log/memory
/3rd-party-relay leakage). Active-MITM by the broker remains a documented
follow-up (needs a secret the broker never sees, e.g. a QR key fragment).

Description: Identified a Private Key, which may compromise cryptographic security and sensitive data encryption.
Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(extension): configurable signer backends (encrypt-at-rest + native gpg-agent)

Introduce a signer-backend abstraction so private-key custody is selectable in
options. The background worker no longer signs directly — it asks a backend:
  async sign(canonicalPayloadString) -> armoredDetachedSignature
  async getFingerprint()             -> fp
The exact CAPAUTH_NONCE_V2 (and V1/CLAIMS) bytes are built by the caller and
signed VERBATIM, so the signed bytes are identical across all backends (Tier B
origin-binding flow unchanged).

Backends (capauth_settings.signerBackend):
  1. local-plaintext  — current paste-key path (fallback, demo-grade).
  2. local-encrypted  — armored key encrypted at rest via WebCrypto PBKDF2
     (SHA-256, 210k iters, random salt) -> AES-GCM (random IV). Only ciphertext
     is stored; decrypted into the in-memory unlock session on UNLOCK. Legacy
     plaintext keys can be migrated (encrypt + delete plaintext).
  3. native-gpg       — key NEVER enters the browser; background.js connects to a
     Chrome Native Messaging host (com.capauth.signer) that signs via OS
     gpg/gpg-agent (loopback pinentry; smartcard/YubiKey supported).

New files:
  lib/keyvault.js          — PBKDF2/AES-GCM encrypt/decrypt envelope (no plaintext).
  lib/signer-backends.js   — interface, 3 backends, connectNative transport, factory.
  native-host/capauth_signer.py     — stdio length-prefixed JSON host (validated, never echoes key).
  native-host/com.capauth.signer.json — manifest template (allowed_origins).
  native-host/install.sh   — registers per-user manifest (Chrome/Chromium/Brave/Edge on Linux; macOS/Windows documented).

Wiring:
  background.js — getSignerBackend(); routed signNonce/signClaims/provider sign
    through the backend; backend-aware UNLOCK (decrypts envelope for encrypted),
    CHECK_STATUS reports backend+needsUnlock, NATIVE_HOST_PING detection.
  options — backend selector (radio) + per-backend panels + encrypt-on-save +
    migration button + native-host status check.
  popup — unlock box keyed on needsUnlock (native-gpg has nothing to unlock).
  manifest(.firefox).json — add nativeMessaging permission.

Tests (vitest): encrypt->decrypt round-trip (right pass decrypts, wrong fails),
encrypted store never contains plaintext, KDF >=210k/SHA-256, canonical V2 bytes
identical across all 3 backends (shared fixture), native-gpg dispatch builds the
correct host message (mocked connectNative) + surfaces errors, locked encrypted
backend refuses to sign. 70 passed (45 baseline + 25 new). Native host verified
e2e against a temp gpg key (sign + gpg --verify over exact bytes).

Docs: README — three backends + §6 security-tradeoff table + native-host
protocol/install paths + follow-ups (NIP-46 phone signer, macOS/Windows host
packaging, hardware-token testing).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Identified a Private Key, which may compromise cryptographic security and sensitive data encryption.
Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(extension): window.capauth provider + Tier B origin-binding (anti-phishing)

Builds the CapAuth browser extension out to deliver the two headline items
from the prior-art research: a NIP-07-style `window.capauth` key-signing API
and Tier B client-attested origin-binding (the real phishing fix).

window.capauth provider (content_scripts/provider.js, MAIN world):
- getFingerprint() and signChallenge(challenge) exposed to pages, frozen.
- signChallenge forwards ONLY the server challenge fields and STRIPS any
  page-supplied origin — the page can never influence what origin is signed.

Tier B origin-binding (the load-bearing change):
- provider_bridge.js (ISOLATED world) re-derives origin = window.location.origin
  (the browser's truth, in a world the page can't reach) and attaches it.
- background.js builds the exact CAPAUTH_NONCE_V2 canonical bytes with that
  origin and signs in the service worker. A phishing proxy at evil.example
  thus signs origin=https://evil.example; the real server rejects invalid_origin.
- The private key + passphrase never enter page scope (WebAuthn-equivalent).

In-browser PGP signing:
- Reuses the vendored OpenPGP.js wrapper (lib/openpgp.js -> openpgp-bundle.js).
- In-memory passphrase unlock session (15 min, never persisted); UNLOCK_KEY/
  LOCK_KEY/UNLOCK_STATUS actions. At-rest key encryption is stubbed (noted).

Popup UX:
- Phishing-resistant origin-consent prompt (shows the REAL requesting origin,
  allow/deny) + key unlock box. background queues per-origin consent requests.

Auto-fill:
- autofill.js (MAIN world) detects the Nextcloud plugin /apps/capauth/login and
  the OIDC IdP /oidc/authorize, fills fingerprint, signs via window.capauth, and
  fills the signature (also dispatches capauth:signed for native login.js).
- Native login.js (Nextcloud) and the OIDC login page now prefer window.capauth
  and fall back to the manual paste flow when the extension is absent.

Tests (vitest, 45 pass / was 34):
- CAPAUTH_NONCE_V2 bytes match the shared cross-impl fixture byte-for-byte.
- origin signed == window.location.origin (mocked), not page-supplied.
- signChallenge produces a signature that verifies with a test PGP key.
- phishing origin yields different bytes AND the relayed signature fails against
  the real server's bytes (relay-replay defeated).
- provider API contract: injection/frozen + origin-stripping forwarding.

Out of scope / follow-up (see browser-extension/README.md): at-rest key
encryption, multi-key, NIP-46 QR remote signer, Firefox MAIN-world port, store
publishing.

Description: Identified a Private Key, which may compromise cryptographic security and sensitive data encryption.
Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(bunker-pwa): vendor OpenPGP.js locally (drop CDN dependency)

Round B. The phone-signer loaded OpenPGP.js from unpkg — a 3rd-party CDN that
can be blocked (it was, on the operator's network) and breaks sovereignty +
offline use. Vendor openpgp.min.js v5.11.3 into phone-signer/vendor/, reference
it locally, precache it in the service worker (cache v3), and serve vendor/*
with a long immutable cache (the 540KB bundle isn't refetched each load) while
app code stays no-cache.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Lumina
Message:
fix(authz): reject unsigned tokens in decide(); fail issuance on signing error

SEC-CRIT bc56b98b. capauth.authz.decide() granted capabilities on a token
that was never signed, including the two skcode RCE rows (skcode.dispatch,
skcode.inject). Reproduced on the live system: issue_token() failed to sign
("gpg: skipped D8920EA8...: No secret key"), printed signed: False, wrote the
token to the store anyway, and decide() then answered allow=True with the
reason "granted: subject enrolled verified with an active token granting ...".

decide() gated on exactly four facts (known capability, enrolled non-revoked
device, enrollment mode >= the rule minimum, a token present/is_active/not
revoked) and never looked at the signature. grep for signature/verify in
authz.py returned zero matches, while the comment at step 5 nevertheless read
"All cryptographic facts satisfied -> allow". The token store is
Syncthing-replicated, so "can write a file into the store" was effectively
"can mint yourself any capability".

Two fixes:

1. decide() now requires the granting token to carry a signature that
   verifies, via the new tokens.signature_verifies(). A token whose signature
   is absent, corrupt, made over different bytes, made by a key other than the
   issuer it declares, or unverifiable because the key is unreachable is
   treated as if it were not there at all. Verification reuses the existing
   manifest.verify_manifest() primitive (gpg --status-fd VALIDSIG parsing, so
   revoked and expired keys never pass), pinned to the payload's issuer
   fingerprint. No new crypto was written.

2. issue_token() and mint_audience_token() now raise TokenSigningError on a
   signing failure and write NOTHING, instead of degrading to an unsigned
   token. Both share one _apply_signature() path, which runs before the token
   is persisted.

Trust anchor, stated plainly: the verifier's local gpg keyring at ~/.gnupg,
which sits outside the replicated ~/.skcapstone store. That is what makes the
check meaningful against a store-write adversary. It does NOT establish that
an issuer is authorized to grant a given capability; issuer is self-declared
and pinned only to the key that actually signed. A trusted-issuer allowlist is
fleet-wide policy and is deliberately left out, since hardcoding one would
break PEPs evaluating tokens issued on other nodes. Documented in both the
authz module docstring and signature_verifies().

Fails closed throughout: unreachable key material denies, it does not pass
through. The misleading step-5 comment is replaced with one describing what
the code actually does and does not assert.

Tests: new tests/test_authz_signature_gate.py (16 tests) runs against REAL
generated OpenPGP keys and covers the required cases: an unsigned token does
not grant skcode.dispatch or skcode.inject; corrupted, byte-tampered,
wrong-signer and unattributable-issuer signatures do not grant; a validly
signed token still grants for both RCE rows and skchat.send, so the fleet does
not brick; and issue_token/mint_audience_token raise with nothing left in the
store. All eight deny-side tests were confirmed to FAIL with the gate removed,
and both issuance tests to FAIL with the raise removed.

Existing suites that asserted an ALLOW were issuing unsigned tokens, which is
exactly the defect, so they now issue SIGNED tokens against a new hermetic
stub_token_signing fixture. That stub fakes only the gpg subprocess and leaves
the real signature_verifies() logic running, so an unsigned or tampered token
still fails there too. test_trust_graph's two calls, which assert graph edges
rather than signing, are now explicitly sign=False.

Suite: 923 passed, 54 skipped (baseline 907/54, plus the 16 new tests; no
change in skip count).
